rationale: This is the archived PayableStretchProfit with the conditioner's rank orientation reversed and the expected sign flipped to match its realized negative alpha — a mechanical in-sample sign fit on an already-evaluated construction rather than a new hypothesis test.

(lct−dlc)/lct is just 1 − dlc/lct, a denominator swap on the already-tested ShortDebtShareProfit (NEG dlc/lt, α=3.4%, t=3.5) and highly collinear with it, so the "mix vs. level" framing does not make this substantively different from an archived winner.

This is the only proposal opening a genuinely untested channel (accounting conservatism rather than funding structure) with a coherent mechanism and full coverage, though the reviewer should be aware that dp/(at−act) is heavily contaminated by asset age, goodwill/intangible-heavy denominators, and is partly a mechanical restatement of EBITDA-based profitability.

(act−dlc)/lct decomposes into act/lct minus dlc/lct, both of which are already-tested conditioners in the archive (IntangibleProfitWithSlack, RolloverRiskAdjustedProfit, SurvivalHorizonProfit uses the identical act−dlc numerator), so this is a recombination of known ingredients rather than a new economic channel.

The Δact/at leg rewards firms accumulating current assets, which is the long leg of the well-documented working-capital accruals/asset-growth anomaly and predicts *low* returns, so the stated positive expected sign is in tension with the expression's dominant known component; the Δdlc leg meanwhile duplicates ShrinkingRolloverExposure.

The conditioner is byte-identical to the archive's best performer (RolloverRiskAdjustedProfit, NEG dlc/act) and only the profitability denominator changes, making this a one-input tweak of an evaluated signal, with the added hazard that at−act goes to zero for asset-light firms and produces unstable, outlier-driven ratios.
